changes: Raises the backend preview worker ceiling from 24 to 80 for high-connection providers.
Starts gallery browsing at the proven v3.6.5 concurrency and ramps upward only while a real thumbnail backlog exists and measured throughput remains healthy.
Reserves roughly 12% of configured NNTP connections for headers, name resolution, and interaction; a 55-connection provider can ramp from 16 toward 48 concurrent previews.
Steps preview concurrency down when thumbnail failures rise or throughput materially regresses instead of blindly saturating the provider.
Closes warm preview NNTP sockets about 3 seconds after a browsing burst goes idle so downloads can reclaim provider sessions quickly.
Immediately returns to the small download-reserve preview budget when active download/retry/cancel traffic appears.
Preserves v3.6.5 Windows taskbar identity reliability and all v3.6.4 package-browser behavior.
